Folks — I ran microbenchmarks and did a quick model of options. High‑level findings (attached sketch: draft-mop-sketch.pdf):

1) Memory profile: your 50k token working set (KV + activations) is ~70–90GB depending on model sharding and quantization. That pushes pure memory‑heavy requests into H100 territory (80GB HBM H100 or multichip). A100 40GB will require tiling/eviction and may increase p95 by 2–4x unless we shard aggressively and rely on async eviction.

2) Throughput vs cost: For 2k token responses at p95 < 600ms: (estimates, include infra and reserved amortized ops)
   - 1 H100 slot (gen‑optimized) can serve ~18–22 long responses/min under our tuned runtime (with int8 quantization on smaller models).
   - 1 A100 (80GB variant, if you can procure 80GB) behaves closer to H100 but with ~10–20% higher latency for equivalent quantized paths. Standard 40GB A100 drops memory headroom and raises eviction complexity.
   - L4 excels for short‑context, high‑QPS but isn’t viable for 50k tokens without model distillation — it’s best used for embeddings, reranking, and side workloads.

3) Operational options:
   - Memory‑first pool: Start with 6 H100 reserved (typical reserve = sustained baseline for production) + 4 H100 burst. This covers baseline traffic with headroom and gives predictable p95.
   - Hybrid pool (cost‑driven): 3 H100 pinned (critical path) + 12 A100 (80GB) for bulk inference. Autoscale rules spike into burst H100 if A100 latency breaches. This reduces committed H100 count but needs carefully tested fallback routing and kernel path parity.
   - Cost‑savings: move non‑critical workloads to L4 fleet (embeddings, offline summarization) — 30–40% unit cost savings compared to H100 for those jobs.

4) Fallback/Canary: canary a mixed pool with 2 H100 for 10% of traffic (latency‑critical), route rest to A100; measure delta over 2 weeks. If p95 delta < 10% then broaden.

I'll attach the sketch with numeric cost examples. Next steps: confirm QPS profile, acceptable commit level (monthly v annual), and whether Cyclone can use 80GB A100 variants.

Anita — brief ops/contract framing and an alternative approach:

- Committed ranges (examples for 12‑month annual commit):
  Option A (Memory‑first): 6 H100 reserved / 4 H100 burst = commit equivalent: 6 slots baseline.
  Option B (Hybrid cost‑first): 3 H100 reserved + 12 A100 (80GB) reserved = commit equivalent: 15 slots but weighted pricing differs.

- Cost variance sensitivity (if traffic +30%):
  Option A: expect ~+25–35% cost if you add burst H100 on demand (bursting metered). Tail latency remains stable.
  Option B: latency risk increases (A100 eviction) — if traffic +30% without adding more H100, p95 could degrade ~40–70% depending on request composition. Bringing up burst H100 will add metered spend but can be automated by Redwood routing policy.

- Ops runbook stub (what we provide):
  1) Telemetry: token‑level latency & memory eviction traces per request; alert when eviction rate > 2%/min.
  2) Fallback routing: policy to move <5% sampled traffic to H100 pool when eviction spikes, automated up to configured burst budget.
  3) Canary plan: 2 H100 dedicated for 14 days at 10% traffic; if p95 delta < 12% expand.
  4) Quantization: recommend int8 for non‑safety‑critical models; we provide regression evals to validate quality impact.

Mutual action plan (proposed milestones):
  - Week 0: Sign MOU & confirm commitment band (we'll draft templates).
  - Week 1–2: Provide full telemetry and workload traces. Redwood provides baseline bench & canary config.
  - Week 3–4: Canary on prod path (2 H100 at 10% traffic).
  - Week 5: Review metrics, decide on expanding H100 or leaning on A100 pool.

If procurement needs a hard cap, Option B with a slightly higher A100 count can reduce headline $ but comes with operational caveats. Happy to walk procurement through numbers on a call.

-Irene

Team — summarizing the recommended path so procurement/engineering can align and we can attach to the MOU:

Summary recommendation (balanced):
- Start with Hybrid canary: 3 H100 reserved (critical) + 8 A100 (80GB) reserved + L4 fleet for non‑critical/embeddings.
  Rationale: reduces headline committed H100 while giving predictable p95 for critical paths. 8 A100 reserved reduces metered burst in normal growth.

Operational controls we will deliver:
- Canary: 2 H100 dedicated for 14 days at 10% traffic (validate p95 & quality).
- Autoscale/burst policy: automated up to 4 additional H100 metered bursts with alerting and budget caps.
- Telemetry: per‑token latency, eviction traces, and rollup dashboard (shared Drive link below).
- Quality gating: Redwood will run regression evals on your holdout prompts for int8 quantized paths.

Procurement asks we need answered to finalize MOU:
1) Commit cadence: monthly vs annual (annual gives best pricing).
2) Ceiling on metered burst spend (example: $X/month).
3) Approval to test 80GB A100 in canary (or confirm A100 40GB only).

Files attached for MOU: cost_projection_Q2.xlsx (budget scenarios), draft-mop-sketch.pdf (ops sketch). I have also linked the Deal JIRA and our analysis folder.
